assumptions: Finite nonempty vertex and coordinate sets, finite edges, nonnegative finite coefficient matrices, spectralRadius of the actual aggregate matrix below one. Gauge allows extended pseudodistances and does not assume completeness or separation.
quantifiers: All actual families F,G and all natural iteration depths n; positive weights and q depend on the aggregate matrix only.
domains: System.Family contains every dependent function on the given node input sets. delta is the supremum over every input, with ENNReal multiplication 0*top=0.
conclusions: One-step and n-step componentwise matrix comparison; strictly positive finite weights; 0<q<1 and M*w<=q*w; contraction in the actual weighted supremum.
representation: PartitionData constructs the typed stop/call System from actual disjoint subsets and transports exactly the stated transform clauses. Option Y is the isolated absorbing extension, linked to any supplied bottom-point presentation by absorbingEquiv. The spectral proof uses a finite power sum, an equivalent constructive alternative to the reference Neumann sum.

assumptions: Scalar metric on Y=X° is exactly sup_i(g.d i), finite and complete; Y is nonempty and all pair distances are bounded by a finite B. Common spectral condition.
quantifiers: One fixed family, uniqueness against every family, and for each arbitrary H a finite C_H and every n.
domains: The ALL-family weighted uniform space, not continuous, bounded, or finitely supported subfamilies.
conclusions: The weighted family space is complete by a proved uniform equivalence to all functions Sigma(Input)->Y with uniform convergence. Diameter makes all weighted distances finite. A unique fixed family exists; max delta(T^n H,F*)<=C_H*q^n with C_H a genuine NNReal.
representation: familyEMetric states the exact distance. Explicit UniformSpace arguments prevent accidentally using the product topology. Both directions of the uniform equivalence are proved Lipschitz using the maximum weight and maximum inverse weight. The metric hypothesis hd is equality with the supplied scalar maximum, not a substitute contraction or completeness certificate.

assumptions: S2 hypotheses; a second terminal function and return functions with exactly the same graph, input sets, stop/call decisions, routed inputs and L_e; finite eta indexed by vertex and coordinate; the specified pointwise local errors.
quantifiers: Every input on each terminal piece, every return input y, and every coordinate; both actual fixed families; no unspecified norm equivalence replaces the vector claim.
domains: The perturbed System literally retains Input,src,dst,L and the selected routed call input. Terminal values are totalized only off terminal pieces, where they are unused.
conclusions: Local delta(TG,Ttilde G)<=eta. Finite fixed-family delta satisfies d<=M*d+eta. The actual real matrix 1-M is proved invertible; d<=(1-M)^(-1)*eta coordinatewise. Both fixed points exist by S2.
representation: The bound records delta!=top for every component before converting it to a real value. A finite-dimensional signed-vector maximum principle proves matrix invertibility and the inverse comparison without cancelling infinite values or assuming a resolvent certificate. The displayed inverse is Matrix.nonsingInv of the actual coefficient matrix.

assumptions: Only the common conditions, with no output completeness, finite family diameter, or separation added.
quantifiers: Refutes the universal conjunction by a legitimate one-node positive-real example with no fixed family.
domains: X° is positive reals, U is the singleton positive value, all input is a call, return y/2; Option supplies bottom.
conclusions: The actual aggregate spectral radius is below one but there is no nonabsorbing fixed family, hence the stated global existence/uniqueness/geometric assertion is false.
representation: positiveSubset transports the typed Unit input onto the actual singleton subset. A second complete but unbounded example is retained in the copied source closure; it is supplementary, not used to smuggle completeness into the common hypotheses.

assumptions: Exactly the prescribed single-node all-call real-output system with b(n)=n+1, a(y)=y/2, and usual real distance.
quantifiers: All fixed families are classified, all real parameters c occur; for every depth k the supremum error of H(n)=n is infinite, while every fixed input converges to zero.
domains: Nat index n represents positive integer n+1. The injective positiveInput identifies the actual subset of R. Families still range over every positive integer.
conclusions: Fixed families are c*2^(n+1) in the zero-based encoding, hence F^c(t)=c*2^t in the task. They are not unique; distinct ones have infinite uniform distance. H evolves as (n+k+1)/2^k, is pointwise convergent, and is never at finite uniform distance from zero.
representation: No terminal piece or extra boundedness restriction is added. Real completeness and exact ordinary metric compatibility are separately recorded. The actual coefficient matrix has spectral radius below one.

assumptions: The finite scalar metric on X° is complete; no diameter bound. The actual finite residual D_w(T H0,H0)!=top is the only branch seed assumption. Positive weights and q<1 are supplied by S1.
quantifiers: Every seed H0 with finite residual; every H within its finite-distance branch; uniqueness is only against fixed families in that branch; every natural n.
domains: branch is exactly {F | weighted(F,H0)!=top}. It is not a finite-support, bounded-output, or preselected fixed-point subspace.
conclusions: Branch is closed and complete, invariant under the actual T, and pair distances within it are finite. A fixed family is constructed and proved unique there; D_w(T^n H,F*)<=q^n*(D_w(H,H0)+R0/(1-q)), with a finite max-delta geometric constant too. Distinct zero-residual fixed seeds in S5 occupy different branches.
representation: Completeness of the full extended metric family space is derived from completeness of Y; closed finite-distance components inherit it. Banach is applied only after proving residual finiteness. The counterexample proves both zero residual and infinite cross-branch distance.

assumptions: Only the original stop/call structure for least partial solutions; spectral assumptions are not needed for this construction. Quantitative counterexamples satisfy the common spectral condition. A common call-depth bound is assumed only in its explicit conditional theorem.
quantifiers: Leastness against every partial fixed family; nonbottom value exactly at finitely terminating inputs; arbitrary initial families and all n>=K+1 under common depth K.
domains: PartialFamily takes Option Y with none as bottom and equality otherwise as the information order. Evaluation traverses the actual deterministic call path.
conclusions: A least fixed family is constructed; it is total iff each input terminates. Pointwise termination does not give a finite geometric uniform bound: countdown has infinite error at every finite k. A common call-depth K gives exact stabilization at K+1. Even depth-one calls do not bound the first error: a real-output system stabilizes at n=2 while its n=1 error is infinite.
representation: countdown is real-output with ordinary metric and return /2; its tail is 2^n/4^k for k<=n. depthOne encodes even terminals and odd calls by Bool×Nat, with an injective real input realization. Thus the negative speed examples use genuine unbounded errors, not a degenerate pseudometric or empty domain.
